query: How should a RAG system be evaluated in production?
report:
## Summary

Retrieval-augmented generation cuts hallucination rates by 43% whenever the retriever returns passages that actually contain the answer.

## Evaluation

The TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation track measures context precision and context recall separately [2]. Published systems rarely use comparable metrics, and evaluation of retrieval-augmented generation pipelines remains fragmented [1].

## Sources considered

Weighed and rejected a vendor blog post that made performance claims without publishing a measurement.

citations.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
citations.content: Combining parametric memory with non-parametric memory through retrieval has become a common approach to knowledge-intensive tasks. Evaluation of retrieval-augmented generation pipelines remains fragmented, with published systems reporting metrics that are rarely comparable across papers. Context precision measures whether the retrieved passages that are ranked highly are actually relevant to the question being asked.
citations.snippet: Combining parametric memory with non-parametric memory through retrieval has become a common approach to knowledge-intensive tasks.

citations.title: TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation Track Overview
citations.content: The TREC Retrieval-Augmented Generation track measures context precision and context recall separately. Context recall asks what fraction of the relevant information required to answer the question was actually retrieved by the system. Context precision asks what fraction of the retrieved information was actually relevant.
